name: Finger Pass
description:
Answer administrator prompts with your fingerprint or your password, whichever comes first.

GNOME makes you wait for the fingerprint reader before it offers the password. Finger Pass replaces the authentication dialog with one that shows the reader and the password field together: touch the reader or start typing. The reader's state is drawn in the dialog, with the attempts left.

The preferences window turns the fingerprint on for administrator dialogs and for sudo in one click (it edits /etc/pam.d/sudo and /etc/pam.d/polkit-1 after asking for your password, keeps the originals, and can undo it), checks your reader, and repairs the setup when a package update takes it away. Login and the lock screen are left alone.
